The text states left cVEMP p13 latency was prolonged from 14.6 ms to 26.1 ms without naming the time points; Table 1 shows 14.6 at Two months and 26.1 at Four months for the left side, and 25.8 at Seven months.

HUT result is Normal at four months in Table 1, whereas the follow-up text says HUT testing suggested persistent autonomic dysfunction and the seven-month cell reads Delayed OH. Parent decision: an ambiguity, not a source conflict (no two values for one cell; 'persistent' is interpretive and the seven-month cell reads Delayed OH).
Authors cannot say whether SARS-CoV-2 directly affected the superior vestibular nerve or triggered VZV reactivation.
The seven-month vHIT gain of 1.96 is called unusually elevated; the authors say technical or reproducibility issues may have contributed and central overcompensation cannot be excluded.

Discussion mentions long COVID-19 neurological sequelae including cognitive impairment (brain fog) and dysautonomia in general terms; cognitive impairment is not documented in the patient narrative or tables.

Discussion states bilateral canal paresis in caloric testing, whereas the initial text describes absent right-ear responses with a residual left-sided response; Table 1 caloric cell reads 0/3.4 with a reference of >10 and no unit. The b00037 paragraph never names this case or the patient, so the statement is not literally attributed (review_only); the difference is an ambiguity, not a conflict.

Table 1 time columns (Two, Four, Seven months) do not state their anchor; the text uses months post-onset for the follow-up tests and says he presented two months after the initial illness. The Two/Four/Seven months headers share one table and so order the column assessments among themselves (p1-e12 -> p1-e09 -> p1-e10), but the Two months column is not equated with the 'Two months later' presentation.
Discussion says prolonged cVEMP latency points to central involvement and raises possible central nervous system involvement, whereas emergency CT and MRI ruled out central pathology at onset.

Treatment with antivertigo medication, adenosine triphosphate, vitamin B12 and vestibular rehabilitation is stated without a time or an order word relative to the initial findings or the four- and seven-month assessments; the emergency CT/MRI is likewise unordered against the swab.
